issues.description: The template's example usage in Main.java constructs Seal, Pig, and Goat with two arguments (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), but the UML/specification and the solution implement these animal constructors with a single parameter (name). This mismatch can cause compilation/runtime confusion when students try to run or follow the provided Main example or when they implement constructors according to the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the example usage in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java consistent with the specification/UML: either change the example to use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")), or adjust the UML/specification and solution to include a second constructor parameter (and corresponding attribute) if the extra 'type' parameter is intended. Updating the template Main to match the UML (single-arg) is the least invasive fix.

issues.description: The template Main.java uses two-argument constructors for animals (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), whereas the problem description/UML and the solution implementation define animal constructors that initialize only the 'name' attribute (single-argument constructors). This mismatch in constructor API (number of parameters/signature) creates a mapping confusion for students about how to implement the classes and their constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage in the template Main.java consistent with the UML/problem statement and solution: use single-argument constructors that accept only the animal 'name' (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). Alternatively, if a second attribute was intended, update the UML/problem statement and solution to include and document that additional attribute so all artifacts match.
